newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine Central Bank chief says peso recovered.
newsitem.headline: Philippine Central Bank chief says peso recovered.

text.p: The Philippine peso had now recovered and was being buoyed by inflows of foreign money after it was hammered by speculators late last week, Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson said on Wednesday.
"The recovery of the peso, the decline of which last Friday was considered temporary and speculative, is due to continued interest by investors in the Philippines," Singson said in a statement.
The peso hit a 27-month low of 26.345 against the dollar last week after a selloff by speculators due to a sharp fall in domestic interest rates triggered by a reserve requirement cut.
The peso had advanced for the third straight day since Friday, posting an average rate of 26.304 in early morning trade on Wednesday from the lowest rate of 26.34 last Friday, the Central Bank said.

Singson acknowledged that the lower interest rates put pressure on the peso. Since the cut in reserve requirements on January 3, Treasury bill yield rates fell by an average of 0.90 percentage point across all maturities, the Central Bank said.

"Such overreaction was negated by strong investor confidence on the Philippines. Large capital flows continue to pour into the country since the beginning of the year as prospects about the Philippine economy remain bright," Singson said.
The government expects the Philippines economy to grow by 7.8 percent this year from about 7.1 percent last year. Inflation is expected at 6.5 percent in 1997 from 8.4 percent in 1996.

The Central Bank said average daily transactions at the Philippine Dealing System (PDS) had now reached $200 million from last year's $110 million. The PDS is the Philippine peso/U.S. dollar computerised trading system among banks.
